conviction_note: No company-level number the market has not seen; a set of small proxies (IoT chip supplier Espressif +33% Q3 revenue, robot-vacuum peers' overseas growth) lean to a modest revenue beat against a single-source $94.5M bar, offset by a company-confirmed semiconductor cost squeeze on gross margin and weak cash conversion; the name's damped reaction history (Q2 2026: +5.8% revenue beat, -0.6% reaction; Q1 2026 flat) and the one-source bar pull p_up to 53, so impact_sum +0.6 and the scaled +0.24 agree in sign and are both near zero.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $94.48M and EPS $0.03 per Earnings Whispers (one source; https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/TUYA/2608242165 family, surfaced via search 2026-11-23). No second agreeing estimate source and no company revenue guide (Tuya gives no numeric guidance: Q2 2026 release https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/tuya-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results-20260825). Bar is therefore treated as unsourced-grade and every size is capped small. Comps: Q3 2025 revenue $82.5M; Q2 2026 $92.9M (+16.0% YoY, beat $87.8M by 5.8%); Q3 2025 was +3% sequential over Q2 2025, which applied to Q2 2026 gives ~$95.7M.
positioning_check: Short interest ~1.5M shares, ~0.24% of shares outstanding, ~3.6 days to cover (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/tuya/shortinterest, latest settlement shown around 2026-11; Stock Market Watch shows 1.5M short / 1.4 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement, https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/TUYA/short-interest). Not crowded. Options: no usable chain (ATM legs not two-sided), skew null, put/call OI 2.07 on only 796 contracts total, so no directional statement from options. Tape: spot $1.46 at the 52-week low, -8.75% over 5 days, -10.98% over 20 days, -43% from the 52-week high, and about -20% since ~$1.83 after the Q2 print (Aug 27). With ~613.3M shares the market cap is ~$895M against $976.1M of cash, deposits and treasuries at 2026-06-30, i.e. the equity trades below its cash.

findings.finding: Espressif (688018.SH), an IoT Wi-Fi/BLE chip and module supplier to the same smart-device makers Tuya's PaaS serves, pre-announced on 2026-10-13 Q3 2026 revenue of RMB 880-900M, +32-35% YoY, with net profit +83-98%; this lands after Tuya last spoke (2026-08-24) and points to strong Q3 IoT connectivity volumes, against a Tuya bar of $94.48M (+14.5% YoY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat consensus by 5.8% ($92.9M vs $87.8M) and the stock moved -0.56% close to close (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/TUYA/q2-2026/); Q1 2026 in line, stock flat. Revenue beats have not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Espressif is an A-share Shanghai name that US ADR holders of TUYA rarely read across; if it had been priced into TUYA, the ADR would not have fallen ~20% since late August and ~9% in the five days into the print. But Espressif itself says smart-home demand was 'relatively flat' and growth came from non-smart-home applications, so the read-through to Tuya's smart-home PaaS is partial.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Roborock/Ecovacs Q3 overseas growth (separate finding, https://wap.eastmoney.com/a/202611023918880863.html) points the same way from a different industry layer.

findings.finding: Chinese smart-home/robot device makers that report after Tuya's August print showed strong overseas Q3 demand: Roborock Q3 2026 revenue RMB 5.614bn, +34.85% YoY (H1 overseas revenue +53.8%), Ecovacs Q3 revenue +10.6% YoY with own-brand overseas revenue +40-47% in H1; relevant to Tuya's PaaS customers (Chinese ODMs/brands shipping abroad) and its smart home & robot product line ($13.5M, 15% of Q2 revenue, +23.2%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same as above: Q2 2026 +23.2% growth in smart home & robot products and +16% total revenue produced a -0.56% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer data from A-share filers; TUYA's ADR drift lower into the print shows no read-across has been taken. Robot-vacuum makers are not Tuya's core PaaS customer set, and the same peers cite memory-chip cost pressure (Ecovacs Q3 net profit down), so the positive is volume, not margin.
findings.independence: Shares the 'Chinese IoT exporters had a strong Q3' theme with the Espressif finding but from a different layer (device makers vs chip supplier) and different documents.

findings.finding: Semiconductor and memory input-cost inflation compressed Tuya's PaaS gross margin to 46.8% in Q2 2026 from 48.7% (overall 46.3% vs 48.4%), the company said costs would stabilise only over the next two to three quarters, and smart-home peers (Ecovacs) blamed Q3 profit declines on memory-chip prices, so Q3 gross margin likely stays below the 48.3% of Q3 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin fell 2.1 points YoY and the stock reacted -0.56%, i.e. the margin dip was absorbed alongside a revenue beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the margin pressure is in the Q2 release. What is not in the price is whether it deepened in Q3 as memory prices kept rising (Notebookcheck July 2026: smart-home hub prices up to +100%, https://www.notebookcheck.net/Rising-costs-in-the-Smart-Home-The-impact-of-the-chip-and-RAM-shortage.1338441.0.html). Tuya passes costs through (gross profit still +11.1% in Q2), which caps the damage and also inflates revenue.
findings.independence: Transcript says most Q2 pricing passed higher input costs through and costs should stabilise in 2-3 quarters (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262129870-tradingkey); same company source family as the release.

findings.finding: Tuya declared a cash dividend with both its Q2 2025 results (Aug 2025, ~$33M) and its Q4 2025 results (Mar 2026, $0.0605/ADS, ~$37M), but the Q2 2026 release (Aug 24, 2026) carried no dividend declaration, breaking the semi-annual pattern, while the equity now trades below its ~$976M cash pile (market cap ~$895M at $1.46 on ~613.3M shares); a capital-return announcement with Q3 (dividend or buyback) is possible but not signalled.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean per-print reaction found for the 2025 dividend declarations; the stock fell ~20% from ~$1.83 (late Aug 2026) after the interim dividend was not declared, consistent with yield holders leaving.
findings.why_not_priced: The skip is public, so the sign of the price drift already reflects no dividend; a declaration with Q3 would be a surprise the ADR at a 52-week low and below net cash is not positioned for. If the market expected a Q3 capital return the stock would not be making new lows into the print. Conversely, if Tuya has moved to one annual dividend with Q4 results, nothing happens on this print, which is why the central size is small.
findings.independence: Dividend history from the Q2 2025 release title (https://tuya.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tuya-reports-second-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and) and the Q4 2025 release (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/tuya-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and-declaration-of-cash-dividend-20260302); share count from Tuya's HKEX monthly return (https://www.itiger.com/news/1171769739). No document says a Q3 declaration is coming.

findings.finding: Operating cash flow fell to $6.2M in Q2 2026 from $18.2M a year earlier (H1 $12.6M vs $27.5M) despite non-GAAP net profit of $18.9M, and cash/investments fell from $1,017.3M (Dec 2025) to $976.1M (June 2026); a second weak cash-conversion quarter would be read as working-capital build tied to pass-through pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 OCF drop was in the August release and the stock moved -0.56% on the day, then about -6% over the following month (allinvestview window to Sep 24).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: flagged publicly after Q2 (Insider Monkey: 'grew revenue 16% but operating cash flow fell 66%'). Only a repeat in Q3 is new; the Dec-to-June cash decline is mostly the ~$37M April dividend, which shrinks this concern.

findings.finding: Into the print the ADR is at a 52-week low ($1.46, -8.75% in 5 days, -11% in 20 days, -43% from the high) with no company-specific cause found since the Q2 release, short interest only ~0.24% of shares (3.6 days), and a 4-analyst Buy consensus with ~$3.2-3.4 targets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a decline to a July 52-week low (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tuya-nysetuya-hits-new-52-week-low-heres-why-2026-07-23/) and the print bought -0.56% on the day and +1.6% over a week.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself; the drawdown has no identified cause, so it is evidence neither of over-reaction nor of a leak. Filed for the panel as context: low expectations and a non-crowded short mean neither a squeeze nor a forced-buyer mechanism.
findings.independence: Analyst consensus https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tuya/ratings; price history from the baseline file.

findings.finding: Simple sequential arithmetic puts Q3 revenue around $95-96M (Q3 2025 was +3% over Q2 2025; Q2 2026 was $92.9M and beat consensus by 5.8%), slightly above the single-source $94.48M bar, with Q3 2025's $82.5M an easy comp (+1.1% YoY then).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats of 5.8% (Q2 2026) and ~0% (Q1 2026) produced -0.6% and ~0% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar itself ($94.48M, Earnings Whispers) already embeds a sequential step-up, so most of this is in consensus; the residual is the company's habit of beating by low-to-mid single digits.
findings.independence: Bar from Earnings Whispers via search (one source); Q2 2026 beat from https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/TUYA/q2-2026/.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-12 Tuya released an open-source skill letting Meta's personal AI agent Muse control devices across 3,000+ categories, an AI-ecosystem headline the call may lean on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI-product headlines (IFA 2026 Doova robot, Tuya Cobuilder) have coincided with continued price declines; no measured reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for 11 days and the stock fell through it; it has no revenue in Q3. Included for completeness only.

baseline_tension: No skew or option-implied move exists; the tape (52-week low, -9% in 5 days) leans negative while the small findings lean slightly positive on revenue and slightly negative on margin, so the evidence neither confirms nor clearly fights the price drift.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; Q2's 5.8% revenue beat bought -0.6%): reported-quarter revenue findings cut, Espressif 0.6->0.4, peers 0.3->0.2, sequential arithmetic 0.3->0.2.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): positioning finding 0.5->0.0, kept filed for the panel.
Lesson 6 (single-source bar): every size kept small; p_up 55->53.
Lesson 3/caveat reaching the number: capital-return finding 0.8->0.5 because no document signals a Q3 declaration; margin finding -0.6->-0.5 because the company passes costs through.
OCF finding and Meta Muse finding unchanged.
